paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between Average Lagging (AL) on the x-axis and BLEU score on the y-axis for four different methods: Consistency-CE, Inconsistency-CE, Inconsistency-CE-MP, and Consistency-Bi. The x-axis, labeled “Average Lagging (AL),” ranges from approximately 2.5 to 11.5 and is scaled linearly with tick marks at 2.5, 5.0, 7.5, and 10.0. The y-axis, labeled “BLEU,” ranges from 25 to 33 and is also linearly scaled, with major gridlines at integer values. The “Consistency-CE” method (purple circles with dashed line) starts at BLEU ≈26.0 at AL=2.5, rises to ≈28.2 at AL=5.0, and reaches ≈31.5 at AL=10.0. The “Inconsistency-CE” method (purple squares with dash-dot line) begins at BLEU ≈26.2 at AL=2.5, increases to ≈29.8 at AL=7.5, and ends at ≈31.7 at AL=10.0. The “Inconsistency-CE-MP” method (blue squares with dashed line) starts at BLEU ≈26.5 at AL=2.5, rises to ≈30.5 at AL=7.5, and reaches ≈32.0 at AL=10.0. The “Consistency-Bi” method (red stars with solid line) begins at BLEU ≈29.0 at AL=2.5, increases to ≈31.3 at AL=7.5, and ends at ≈32.3 at AL=10.0. All methods show a generally increasing trend in BLEU score as Average Lagging increases, with “Consistency-Bi” consistently achieving the highest BLEU scores across the range.
